source.title: Sparse Autoencoder Decomposition of Clinical Sequence Model Representations: Feature Complexity, Task Specialisation, and Mortality Prediction
source.authors: Chris Sainsbury; Feng Dong; Andreas Karwath

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports measurements of SAE features in a clinical sequence model, not neuron poles or explanations tested on held-out activations. Its results do not test any listed claim version.
record.gate_note: The reported feature-complexity measurements concern SAE dictionary features, not individual neuron poles. The paper explicitly describes category-level coherence as weaker than monosemanticity. It does not test explanations on activations they were not written from, report automated explanation scores, or build attribution graphs.
record.test_reason: The paper trains TopK SAEs on a 14.5M-parameter clinical sequence model and measures SAE feature complexity, probe performance and perturbation effects. It never examines individual neurons or neuron poles, never scores neuron explanations, never builds neuron attribution graphs, and does not mention the essay or the automated-explanation paper. None of its results bear on any listed version. Its only link to the topic is general SAE/monosemanticity literature, so 'cites_only' fits better than 'discusses'.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also conclude three further things. First, under full-sequence simple probes, SAE features beat dense representations for mortality but lose for length of stay. Second, at leakage-safe windows, dense representations match or exceed SAE features. Third, delta-mode perturbation cuts noise about 86×, but feature-ablation effects were not formally significant.
record.recipe_differences: TopK SAE decomposition of a 14.5-million-parameter clinical sequence model's residual stream; it does not measure neuron poles or test neuron explanations.
record.method_sensitivity: Feature complexity differs between layer 0 and layer 6; feature reproducibility also varies by layer, with lower matching at deeper layers.

fits_no_version.finding: In FlatASCEND, INSPECT SAE features go from near-token detectors at layer 0 (45.7% singleton, 2.9 tokens/feature) to multi-token features at layer 6 (0.5% singleton, 29.9 tokens/feature). At layer 6, 92.2% stay >50% within one coarse clinical category.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In a small clinical sequence model, SAE dictionary features become more distributed with depth, while mostly retaining coarse category coherence.

fits_no_version.finding: Cross-seed SAE feature reproducibility falls with depth: 42.3% at layer 0, 21.0% at layer 6 and 19.8% at layer 9 (Supp. Table S5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE dictionary features in a small model are largely unstable across seeds, especially in deeper layers.

record.code_released: https://github.com/csainsbury/ascend-flat (currently private; contact the corresponding author for collaborator access)
record.problems: All findings are from one 14.5-million-parameter model architecture. Feature stability across seeds is 21% at layer 6, and downstream seed-wise variability was not formally quantified. Category groupings are coarse and the authors state that category-level coherence is weaker than monosemanticity.
record.rows_left_out: Other results, including mortality prediction, length-of-stay probes, perturbation experiments, and feature reproducibility, do not measure neuron-pole interpretability or explanation accuracy and were not included as rows.

untested.parts: Neuron-pole shares across language models, dense and MoE, at scale.
InceptionV1 polysemantic neurons and the pose / recursive-generalization reading.
Whether interpretable-neuron share depends on architecture, regularization and tools.
Neuron-based attribution graphs without a replacement model.
Whether explanations fit to activating examples predict firing on held-out data.
Simulation-based automated scoring of neuron explanations.

record.verdict_notes: All rows concern SAE features, not neurons, and are correctly linked to 'none'. The study is not one of the original sources. Relation changed from 'discusses' to 'cites_only', because the paper does not engage the neuron-cleanliness claim at all. It only notes that category coherence is weaker than monosemanticity in the SAE literature.

versions.untested_parts: Neuron-pole job shares in Qwen3-32B or comparable models.
Neuron-pole shares across language models, dense and mixture-of-experts architectures, or model scales.
InceptionV1 cat-and-car neurons, pose detection, or recursive generalization.
Neuron interpretability shares in InceptionV1-sized vision models, and whether architecture, regularization, or tools cause changes in those shares.
Attribution graphs built from a large model's own neurons and their behavioral reconstruction.
Whether explanations fit to activating examples predict where neurons fire on unseen activations.
Automated scoring of neuron explanations by simulated activations on new text.
